display.title: Tanya Shiur 34: Chapters 21 and 22, Hashem's Speech Never Leaves Him
display.summary_short: Two Yiddish Tanya classes: chapter 21 on how Hashem's 'speech' stays one with Him, and chapter 22 on how kelipah gets its life 'from behind', with stories and parables.
display.summary_long: Shiur 34 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series holds two weekly classes. The first reviews chapter 20: speech, thought and the soul, and how a tzaddik's thought is not bound by time or place, shown by the story of the Chassid Rabbi Shmuel Levitin, lost in a snowstorm while being moved between Soviet prisons, whose exact location the Frierdiker Rebbe described at a farbrengen. It then studies chapter 21: a person's words leave him, but Hashem's speech remains united with Him even after creation. Parables include a teacher teaching a small child aleph-beis, electricity stepped down by transformers, a father hiding behind a curtain, and the halachah that one cannot cover one's own head with one's own hand. The second class studies chapter 22: kelipah receives life only 'from behind', like a debt thrown over the shoulder to an enemy. It explains spitting at Aleinu, loving every Jew because Hashem loves him, the Zohar's parable of the king who sends a tempter to test his son, eating versus swallowing, and why pride is like idol worship.
display.lesson: Nothing exists apart from Hashem; the more a person sets aside his own sense of self, the more the Shechinah can rest on him.

date.note: No date cues in the audio. Between shiur 30 (Tishrei 5737) and shiur 35 (just after Shavuos, probably 5737).

study_text.note: Review of the end of ch. 20; ch. 21 in the first class, ch. 22 in the second.

segments.title: Review of Tanya chapter 20: speech, thought and the soul
Rabbi Shmuel Levitin lost in the snowstorm
segments.summary: A Chassid escapes a stranded prison wagon in a forest, and the Frierdiker Rebbe describes at a farbrengen exactly where he is.

segments.title: Tanya chapter 21: Hashem's speech stays one with Him
segments.summary: Human speech separates from the speaker, but Hashem's speech stays united with Him; tzimtzum explained with parables of a teacher, electricity and a curtain.

segments.title: Why your own hand cannot cover your head
segments.summary: The halachah about covering one's head for a brachah shows that one cannot conceal oneself from oneself, and Hashem's concealment is not real to Him.

segments.title: Second class: review of chapters 20 and 21
Tanya chapter 22: life 'from behind' and the kelipos
segments.summary: Kelipah receives life only indirectly, as from behind; pride and feeling oneself separate are like idol worship.

segments.title: Spitting at Aleinu and loving every Jew
segments.summary: Why we spit at Aleinu, a Midrash about a man who carried an idol out of Egypt, and why loving Hashem means loving every Jew he loves.

segments.title: The Zohar's parable of the king's son and the tempter
segments.summary: A king hires a tempter to test his son, and the tempter himself hopes the son will refuse.

segments.title: Eating versus swallowing; Pharaoh's lean cows
segments.summary: Holiness absorbs Hashem's life like food that is chewed, while kelipah swallows it whole without benefit.

quality.notes: Two weekly classes joined in one file: the first ends about 58:10 ('next week'), the second opens 'last week we finished chapter 21'. Loshn-koydesh quotations are garbled by ASR.
